prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance forward, passes the right arm around uke's lower back, overlaps with uke, and, using the extension of both knees, the hikite (pulling hand) and the right arm passed around behind, loads uke onto the hips and throws uke forward. Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall) From kumi-kata, tori turns in, loads uke on the hips and throws forward; uke lands and takes ukemi.

How to take the ukemi: Uke rotates sideways about the right foot and takes yoko-ukemi (side breakfall). Tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki and throws uke forward without lifting uke off the mat. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) and throws uke forward without lifting uke up. How to take the ukemi: In time with tori's ō-goshi, uke does not pull the hips back and takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall).

From kumi-kata, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki, loads uke onto the hips and throws forward. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) to break uke's balance forward, and throws uke forward.

heading.en: Devising the practice: practice of tai-sabaki (body movement) and balance

prose.en: Two students practise the body movement together. Practise the tai-sabaki (body movement) in pairs. Cooperation of uke: So that tori does not bend forward, uke arches the upper body moderately even when lifted. Practise loading uke onto the hips and holding the balance.

Tori pushes uke; as uke plants the feet and holds ground, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki and throws with ō-goshi. Push uke, and at the moment uke stands firm, apply ō-goshi (major hip throw) with mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement). As uke pushes, tori turns in with ushiro-mawari-sabaki and applies ō-goshi. In time with uke pushing forward, apply ō-goshi (major hip throw) with ushiro-mawari-sabaki (backward turning body movement).

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori should not push the hips in too deeply. Tori should not let the stance become too narrow. Uke turns sideways while receiving the technique. Uke should not receive the technique while facing sideways.
Do not apply the technique bent forward, in a posture that drives the head into the mat.
If tori bends at the waist and applies the technique with the head lowered, there is a risk that not uke but tori will injure the neck from the head being driven in.

Prohibit applying the technique with the head lowered; instruct that, if tori loses balance and ends up in a low posture, they release the lapel and sleeve of uke that they are holding and take mae-ukemi (front breakfall) themselves.

With a right-handed grip, it is important that tori raises the upper body and repeats kakari-geiko and yakusoku-geiko so as to break uke's balance to the right front corner before applying the technique, thereby building proficiency.
